reason: E1 supports the premise that additive manufacturing introduces defects and tensile stress, and E2 supports that hybrid manufacturing improves accuracy and that ultrasonic impact refines grains and converts tensile to compressive stress. However, the cited evidence does not directly address micro-forging, laser shock, or shot peening, nor does it demonstrate improved wear or corrosion resistance from these specific techniques.
premises: Additive manufacturing alone produces residual tensile stress, micro-defects, and cracks
Surface strengthening techniques (micro-forging, laser shock, shot peening) can refine microstructure and introduce compressive stress
Combining additive manufacturing with subtractive manufacturing improves part accuracy
Hybrid manufacturing can reduce tensile stress and transform it into compressive stress
These microstructural and stress-state changes improve wear and corrosion resistance
